newsitem.title: UK: Greycoat has not rejected Moorfield.
newsitem.headline: Greycoat has not rejected Moorfield.

text.p: UK property development and investment group Greycoat said on Monday that contrary to weekend newspaper reports, it had not rejected merger proposals by UK property group Moorfield Estates Plc.
"Greycoat still awaits the clarification it has already requested," it said in a statement.
Greycoat's advisers have told Moorfield that they would only provide the due diligence information requested when they were satisfied that the proposal had merit.

Moorfield, whose market capitalisation of 20.7 million pounds is about 10 times smaller than that of Greycoat, has said that a merger would provide better growth prospects for investors in both companies.
The offer comes at a time when Greycoat is fighting break-up proposals from UK Active Value, a fund run by controversial South African investor Brian Myerson and Julian Treger.

Moorfield said earlier today that talks between the two companies were not progressing, adding that in the light of what it called Greycoat's "obduracy", Moorfield would continue talks with "certain shareholders".

Rebel shareholder Myerson, who has led the assualt on Greycoat's board, wants Greycoat to sit down and talk to Moorfield, saying that holders of about 40 percent of Greycoat shares back Moorfield plans.
